quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Dejounte Murray is out to celebrate the birth of his son
quotes.excerpt: he's celebrating the birth of his son and he's being there with his family

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: We just found out Dejounte Murray scratched for personal reasons. Is there anything you can share?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: He's celebrating the birth of his son and he's being there with his family around his family. It's an exciting time for him and his family. quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Keys to tonight's game against the Sacramento Kings
quotes.excerpt: understanding the way that Jokic plays versus the way Sabonis plays, they're both used as a hub

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: What will be some of the keys tonight?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: There's a lot of similarities, understanding the way that Jokic plays versus the way Sabonis plays. They're both used as a hub and guys play off of him. Just being able to understand the assignments that we have, how we can get over screens, how we got to navigate the screens. His aggression in the pick and roll as well as the dribble handoff, being able to tighten up and shrink the floor the best as we can. Then you got guys in Ayo Dosunmu as well as LaVine who are certified quick scorers. Our ability to keep them under control, finish possessions, but then not get into the rat race game of just going back and forth and being able to play our style of basketball.

quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley breaks down the keys to tonight's game against the Kings, emphasizing the need to navigate screens and shrink the floor against a hub-style offense similar to Jokic.

structured.context: Head coach Jamahl Mosley discusses the keys to the game against the Sacramento Kings and mentions defensive assignments.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Expectations for Jeremiah Robinson-Earl as a starting point guard
quotes.excerpt: I expect him to be a dominant point guard that controls and sets the table for others

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: With no Murray and no pool, what does it just sort of mean for Jeremiah as far as what do you expect from him tonight?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: I expect him to be a dominant point guard that controls and sets the table for others. Picks and chooses his moments when he can be aggressive to attack to score, but just being at that facilitator that can one defensively be the head of the snake to guard and pick up full court and then the other side of it is getting distributing and getting us organized on that court.

quotes.social_post: With Dejounte Murray out, Jamahl Mosley expects Jeremiah Robinson-Earl to be a dominant point guard tonight, acting as the facilitator and the head of the snake on defense.

structured.context: Head coach Jamahl Mosley outlines his expectations for Jeremiah Robinson-Earl as he takes on point guard duties for the game.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Evaluating Jeremiah Robinson-Earl's playmaking and distribution
quotes.excerpt: I think he's done an excellent job of distributing. Obviously there's times that he's going to have the ball

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: What have you thought about what you've seen when he has the ball and he's dictating the offense?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: I think he's done an excellent job of distributing. Obviously there's times that he's going to have the ball, we're running plays for him and you can find a matchup that works. They usually have size on him, so then pick and rolls with a small or him bringing the ball up and initiating our offense is also going to be key. That's going to be a team job tonight to be able to find and get ourselves settled and understanding exactly when that ball is in your hand you become the facilitator, the playmaker, no matter who it is in these moments.

quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on Jeremiah Robinson-Earl's playmaking role: He has done an excellent job of distributing and the team will need to work together to get settled and initiate the offense tonight.

structured.context: Head coach Jamahl Mosley evaluates Jeremiah Robinson-Earl's performance as a playmaker and facilitator for the team.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Managing team body language and morale during a losing streak
quotes.excerpt: I don't want nobody sitting around whistling and singing happy songs when you're 0 and 4

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified speaker
text_blocks.text: How do you maybe get ahead of some of the issues body language, things you might see on film to correct address and stay ahead of those problems?

text_blocks.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
text_blocks.text: One is not to overreact. When I talk about body language, nobody's going to be happy to be 0 and 4. I don't want nobody sitting around whistling and singing happy songs when you're 0 and 4. So there's a there's a mood that you can have with not getting the result that you want in those moments. But there's also a way that you bounce out of it and then that becomes the encouragement to your teammate when they check in the game and they check out the game that you now have to fill somebody else up with the encouragement when they step in the game and that's how that energy can transfer over.

quotes.social_post: Addressing the team's 0-4 start, Jamahl Mosley says he does not expect players to be happy, but emphasizes the importance of maintaining positive energy and encouraging teammates to bounce back.

structured.context: Head coach Jamahl Mosley addresses how the team manages body language and morale during their current losing streak.
